Gaurīkuṇḍa
------------------------------------------
Pilgrimage to the Himālayan shrines at Kedāra and Badarī (Garhwal district of Uttaranchal) has been a great dream to many a Hindu even from the very early times.
कैलास">Gaurīkunḍa near Mount KailāsaGaurīkuṇḍa, situated 13 kms. (8 miles) below the Kedārnāth temple, is one of the places the pilgrims do not miss. गौरी or पार्वती is believed to have been born here. There is a nice temple here dedicated to her.
There are also two kuṇḍas or ponds of water, one containing hot water and the other, cold. The latter is called ‘Amṛtakuṇḍa’ and पार्वती is said to have bathed here.
There is also a temple of राधा-कृष्ण.
The climb to Kedārnāth temple from here is quite steep.
There is another गौरीकुण्ड in Tibet, to the east of the Mount कैलास. Situated at a height of 5520 metres (18,400 ft.), it is an elliptical lake 1.2 kms. (0.75 mile) long and 0.8 km. (0.5 mile) wide. It is believed to be 25 metres (84 ft.) deep. It is always covered by ice blocks. Pilgrims take bath here while proceeding towards the मानस-सरोवर and the Mount कैलास.

Gaurī
(‘The white one’)
------------------------------------------
‘Gaurī’ is another name of पार्वती, the consort of शिव. (See PĀRVATĪ for more details.) She is described as a girl of ten years.
She may be worshipped along with शिव as Candraśekhara or as an independent deity. In the former case she is shown as standing on a lotus seat, to his left. She is dark-blue in complexion, three-eyed and two-armed. She holds a blue-lotus in her right hand.
Works like the Aparājitāsūtra mention several forms of गौरी such as Umā, पार्वती, ललिता, Kṛṣṇā and Śrī. The number of these forms varies from 12 to 24.
